public_health_question.v: Can a real-time dynamic model forecast the size and duration of a measles outbreak in a Chicago migrant shelter, and how much did mass vaccination and active case-finding reduce the chance of a large outbreak?

ev.q: CDC created dynamic measles models to forecast outbreak size and duration among shelter residents and quantitatively assess the impact of public health interventions.
Real-Time Use of a Dynamic Model To Measure the Impact of Public Health Interventions on Measles Outbreak Size and Duration
Prompt mass vaccination and active case-finding likely substantially reduced the likelihood of a large measles outbreak in Chicago.

CDC simulated a measles outbreak among shelter residents using a dynamic disease model, updated in real time as additional cases were identified
